item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"medium","summary":"B is the preferable patch because it confines replayability changes to FilesService and keeps request construction and response handling centralized. Neither patch fully satisfies the frozen contract, but A introduces a much broader retry-layer behavior change and duplicates Add's implementation inside Upload.","reasons":["A changes RawClient.Do for every io.Reader request, despite the contract explicitly excluding unrelated request/retry refactoring. This also changes buffering, read-error timing, and streaming behavior across the SDK.","A's Upload reimplements Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing through Add, creating the exact duplication the contract seeks to avoid.","B factors common behavior into one private add method, so Add and Upload at least share option handling, request construction, decoding, and errors, although Upload does not literally call Add as required.","B's Upload retry test uses an os.File source and verifies multipart field name, filename, and content on every attempt. A's Upload retry test uses strings.NewReader and therefore does not directly cover the requested streamed-content case."],"risks_a":["The global RawClient buffering change unnecessarily affects Files.Update and all other reader-bodied requests.","WithNoRetry now changes whether source readers are eagerly consumed, creating new cross-cutting semantics outside the requested API.","Upload duplicates Add internals and may drift as Add evolves."],"risks_b":["Upload calls the new private add helper rather than the existing public Add method, violating the contract's literal delegation requirement.","Add now always buffers its input, changing the preserved lower-level API's streaming and error-timing behavior.","The added tests do not explicitly cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader errors as required."]}
